answer_html: Yes, it works at 1 G. With B along the tweezer polarisation and the imaging polarisation about 50° away, N=1 scatters 0.46×10⁶ photons/s per unit s_tot, against 0.42×10⁶ at zero field. A 99% histogram needs the same ≈508 photons (η = 2%) either way. The one geometry to avoid is imaging polarisation parallel to B, which leaves 8 dark states that nothing remixes.

The cross talk on N=0 does not care about the field. The imaging light is 19 GHz from the nearest N=0 line, so PRaman = rR·stot·T with rR = 0.20 s⁻¹ at both 0 and 1 G. That is about 4.4×10-7 Raman events per imaging photon. Parity forbids an N=0 molecule from ever landing in the bright peak.

Rapid optimum, η = 2%: s_tot = 4, Δ = -2 MHz, U₀ = 1.0 mK, T = 313 µs gives F = 99% with PRaman = 2.5×10-4 per image. Going ten times slower (s_tot = 0.3, T = 3.7 ms) only lowers it to 2.2×10-4. η = 4%: 257 µs and 1.0×10-4.

Why the trade-off is so flat: with 12 ground and 4 excited sublevels the line barely saturates. Photons per unit fluence fall only from 0.46 to 0.39×10⁶ between s_tot = 0.1 and 4. So intensity × time for a fixed photon number is nearly constant, and speed is almost free up to s_tot ≈ 4. Heating out of the trap (≈0.9 µK per photon) and trap-light loss cap the fidelity at ≈99.2% (η = 2%) and ≈99.7% (η = 4%).
assume_html: Molecule: X(N≤3) hyperfine + Zeeman Hamiltonian (Childs 1981 constants); A(J′=½,±), A(J′=3/2,−) in case (a); Γ = 2π×8.29 MHz; b₀₀ = 0.975; v=1,2 repumped via A(v=0) at 2π×1 MHz; 2.5×10⁻⁵ leak to v≥3 per photon.

Tweezer: 780 nm, w₀ = 1 µm, imaging depth U₀ = 1–2.5 mK (scanned), T₀ = 40 µK. N=1 tensor polarisability spread 20% of U₀ (Burchesky et al. 2021). X–A differential scalar shift 5 MHz/mK (unknown; see sensitivity).

Imaging light: retro-reflected beam ⊥ tweezer, two passes added incoherently; linear polarisation 50° from the tweezer's; four sidebands with power 2:1:2:3 (J=½F=1, F=0, J=3/2 F=1, F=2), offsets +1, −1, +2, −2 MHz. Exactly equal detunings create accidental coherent dark states.

N=1 dynamics: 17-level Lindblad OBE (secular), within 3–8% of the full multi-frequency model. The Monte-Carlo interpolates R(Δ, local intensity) along classical trajectories with recoil kicks, Doppler shifts and escape.
Losses: trap-light-induced loss 4×10⁻⁵ per photon at 1.5 mK, scaled with depth (from 90% retention after 2700 photons in Λ-imaging, arXiv:1807.00740).

Detection: η = photon collection × transmission × QE; photon-counting camera; stray light ζ = 10⁻³ of a two-level scatterer's collected light, plus 0.01 dark counts/ms; fidelity from the best threshold with a 50/50 prior.

N=0 cross talk: Kramers–Heisenberg amplitudes through A(J′=½,−) at 19.2 GHz and A(J′=3/2,−) at 52 GHz, summed coherently. If the A(J′=½) Λ-doublet order is reversed, Δ₀ = 21.9 GHz and the Raman rate drops by ×0.77.
